rows.passage_en: For a fixed number N of ideal-gas particles, pressure P, volume V and absolute temperature T satisfy PV = NkT.
rows.review_note: Researcher ratio: P_new/P_old=2/8=1/4.

rows.source_locator: equation 39.22; sections on equilibrium and mean kinetic energy
rows.passage_en: The ideal-gas relation is PV = NkT. Gases at the same temperature have the same average translational kinetic energy per molecule.
rows.review_note: Pressure depends on N as well as temperature and volume; identical containers do not specify equal molecule counts.

rows.source_locator: mirror sign conventions following equation 27.3; plane-mirror limit
rows.passage_en: A plane mirror forms a virtual image the same perpendicular distance behind the mirror as the object is in front.
rows.review_note: Researcher application of the mirror equation with infinite radius: object-to-image separation is twice the object-to-mirror distance, giving 200 cm.

rows.passage_en: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity. A point at radius r sweeps arc length r times its angular displacement.
rows.review_note: Integrate constant angular acceleration from rest: theta=alpha*t^2/2=16 rad and distance=0.1*16=1.6 m.

rows.source_locator: elementary charge row; electron sign is standard charge convention
rows.passage_en: The elementary electric charge has magnitude 1.602176634 × 10^-19 coulombs. An electron carries the negative of this charge.
rows.review_note: One coulomb divided by the elementary charge is about 6.24*10^18 electrons, nearest offered value 6.25*10^18.

rows.passage_en: A spring oscillator’s amplitude depends on both its displacement and velocity at a given instant. Its natural angular frequency satisfies omega^2 = k/m.
rows.review_note: Using horizontal momentum conservation when an equal stationary mass sticks gives v_new=v/2 and omega_new=omega/sqrt(2). Thus A_new^2=x^2+v^2/(2*omega^2), so the effect depends on the collision phase.

rows.passage_en: Gauss’s law relates the total electric flux through a closed surface to enclosed charge divided by vacuum permittivity.
rows.review_note: Symmetry is useful for calculating a field, but is not required for the law to hold.

rows.passage_en: The magnetic part of the Lorentz force is q times the cross product of velocity and magnetic field. It is perpendicular to velocity and does no work.
rows.review_note: The field alone changes the direction, not the proton’s speed. The initial angle affects the path.

rows.source_locator: equation 27.12; real and virtual image discussion
rows.passage_en: A converging lens can form a real image for an object outside its focal length and a virtual image for an object inside that focal length.
rows.review_note: Researcher classification from 1/s+1/s_prime=1/f and the real/virtual sign convention, assuming an ordinary convex lens in air.

rows.source_locator: introductory pendulum discussion; researcher dynamics derivation
rows.passage_en: A pendulum is an oscillator. With fixed gravitational acceleration and fixed release angle, its period scales with the square root of its length and not its mass.
rows.review_note: Researcher dimensional reduction of the pendulum equation from Newton’s law; the familiar small-angle form is T=2*pi*sqrt(L/g). The scaling with length also holds at fixed finite amplitude.

rows.passage_en: For planets orbiting the Sun, orbital period squared is proportional to orbital semimajor axis cubed. In Earth-year and au units, P^2 = a^3.
rows.review_note: For the stated 0.2-year approximation, a=(0.2^2)^(1/3)=0.342 au, closest to 1/3 au.

rows.source_locator: Newton’s Second Law; researcher incline projection
rows.passage_en: Acceleration is net force divided by mass. For frictionless sliding down the same incline, the gravitational force along the slope is proportional to mass.
rows.review_note: Researcher projection: a=g*sin(theta), independent of mass and shape when the objects do not rotate.

rows.passage_en: Without air resistance, an object near Earth has constant downward gravitational acceleration, independent of horizontal motion.
rows.review_note: Integrating vertical acceleration from zero vertical speed gives h=g*t^2/2, hence about four seconds for 80 m.

rows.passage_en: During an interaction, the two bodies exert equal and opposite forces on one another. Each body’s acceleration is its force divided by its mass.
rows.review_note: If the truck is twice as massive, the car’s acceleration has twice the magnitude and the opposite direction.

rows.passage_en: For a fixed quantity of ideal gas at constant temperature, the product of pressure and volume remains constant.
rows.review_note: Researcher ratio: 1e5 Pa * 20/5=4e5 Pa.

rows.source_locator: summary component equations F_x=m*d^2x/dt^2 and F_y=m*d^2y/dt^2
rows.passage_en: In ideal projectile motion near Earth, gravity provides a constant downward acceleration. The horizontal and vertical components obey their own force equations.
rows.review_note: Researcher integration: vertical speed decreases to zero on ascent and increases in magnitude on descent. Total speed at the apex is not zero when horizontal velocity is nonzero.

rows.source_locator: string modes and lambda=2L for the fundamental
rows.passage_en: For a stretched string with fixed ends, a standing-wave mode fits an integer number of half-wavelengths into the string length.
rows.review_note: If the driving wavelength does not fit this condition, 60 Hz is not a normal-mode frequency.

rows.passage_en: The ideal parallel-plate capacitance is proportional to plate area and dielectric constant, and inversely proportional to plate separation.
rows.review_note: C=kappa*epsilon0*A/d: moving plates closer increases capacitance.

rows.passage_en: In electrostatic equilibrium the field inside a metal is zero. Immediately outside a smooth conductor surface, the normal field is local surface-charge density divided by vacuum permittivity.
rows.review_note: The near-surface relation is local and does not require uniform charge distribution.

rows.passage_en: A magnetic force on a charged particle is q(v cross B). When velocity is parallel to the field, this cross product is zero.
rows.review_note: Assume the ideal interior field of a solenoid is axial and there is no electric field; the proton continues at constant velocity.

rows.passage_en: From the magnetic force relation F=qvB for perpendicular motion, a tesla has dimensions N/(A m), because a coulomb equals an ampere-second.
rows.review_note: Dimensional derivation: N/(A*m)=kg/(C*s)=J/(A*m^2). A*N/V has different dimensions. This checks units, not numerical conversion.

rows.source_locator: Newton’s force balance; researcher coordinate projection
rows.passage_en: For a stationary object on a plane inclined at angle theta, the normal force balances the component of gravity perpendicular to the plane: mg cos(theta).
rows.review_note: The cosine dependence decreases nonlinearly as the angle rises while the object remains at rest.

rows.passage_en: Coulomb’s force between fixed charges depends on the charges and their separation. The masses of the charged bodies do not appear in this electrostatic relation.
rows.review_note: Doubling only one mass leaves the electric force unchanged at 50 microNewtons.

rows.source_locator: conservation of energy; researcher symmetric-gravity application
rows.passage_en: When only conservative gravity acts, mechanical energy is conserved. A body released from rest can regain its initial gravitational potential at an equal-height turning point.
rows.review_note: For an ideal evacuated tunnel through a nonrotating, symmetric Earth, the object passes the center and turns at the opposite opening, repeatedly. Real-Earth complications are excluded by the question’s idealization.

rows.source_locator: equilibrium and average kinetic-energy discussion, equations 39.19–39.22
rows.passage_en: Collisions exchange molecular kinetic energy. At thermal equilibrium, the mean translational kinetic energy is determined by temperature rather than molecular species.
rows.review_note: The kinetic-theory source is an idealized model; applying energy exchange to the liquid mixture is a researcher interpretation of the same thermal-equilibrium principle. No equality of individual molecular energies is claimed.

rows.passage_en: A downward-falling object experiences gravity downward and drag upward. Its downward acceleration is the net downward force divided by mass and falls toward zero as drag grows.
rows.review_note: For the question’s linear drag, a=g-bv/m: while below terminal speed, v increases and a decreases. NASA illustrates quadratic drag; the linear-drag formula is a researcher adaptation explicitly stipulated by the question.

rows.source_locator: mode wavelengths; researcher acoustic-pipe boundary-condition derivation
rows.passage_en: Standing-wave resonances satisfy boundary conditions. Adjacent resonant lengths of a pipe with the same end conditions differ by half a wavelength.
rows.review_note: Researcher extension of standing-wave mode quantization to a pipe: compare consecutive resonances rather than the vibrating guitar-string wavelength. End correction cancels approximately in the length difference.

Published key C includes statement II, but at the apex the speed-dependent drag vanishes while gravity remains, so acceleration is not zero. Under the standard model only statement I is true, corresponding to option A. Exclude or independently adjudicate; do not silently relabel.

AC voltage times current is apparent power. Real input power also depends on power factor, which is not specified for the motor. The key assumes unity power factor. Hold for a clearly specified replacement rather than importing this assumption.

Option D contains an extra literal (E) label. The intended physics is consistent, but this competing label could cause parsing artifacts in a four-option study. Prefer a replacement or an explicitly documented display repair.

note: Facts are researcher paraphrases; derivations and assumptions are disclosed. No final approval.
